body.en: Before the trial balance is prepared, a one-sided error is corrected by simply debiting or crediting the affected account with an explanatory note. If the error is found after the trial balance has been prepared with a suspense account, the other side of the *rectifying* entry is the suspense account.

say.en: The credit side was short by 900, so 900 was put on the credit side as a suspense account.
Sales book undercast by 500: credit sales 500 more; the other side is suspense.

Debits 900 equal the credit 900. The suspense account closes with no balance.

body.en: When the trial balance does not agree and the errors cannot be found at once, the difference is placed on the shorter side in a *suspense account*. As each one-sided error is found, its rectifying entry passes through suspense. When all errors are rectified, the suspense account closes automatically.

problem.en: The trial balance of Ashok & Co. had its credit side short by ₹900, which was put to a suspense account. Later these errors were found: (i) the sales book was undercast by ₹500; (ii) rent of ₹200 was posted to the rent account as ₹600. Pass rectifying entries and show that suspense closes.

steps.en: Suspense opens on the credit side with ₹900.
(i) Sales credited ₹500 short: Suspense A/c Dr ₹500 To Sales A/c ₹500.
(ii) Rent debited ₹400 too much: Suspense A/c Dr ₹400 To Rent A/c ₹400.
Suspense: credit 900; debits 500 + 400 = 900. Balance nil, so the account is closed.

answer.en: Suspense Dr 500 / Sales Cr 500; Suspense Dr 400 / Rent Cr 400; suspense account closes.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. The trial balance of Ashok & Co. had its credit side short by ₹900, which was put to a suspense account. Later these errors were found: (i) the sales book was undercast by ₹500; (ii) rent of ₹200 was posted to the rent account as ₹600. Pass rectifying entries and show that suspense closes.

say.en: Let us work this out together. The trial balance of Ashok & Co. had its credit side short by 900, rupees which was put to a suspense account. Later these errors were found: i the sales book was undercast by 500 rupees; ii rent of 200 rupees was posted to the rent account as 600 rupees. Pass rectifying entries and show that suspense closes.
Suspense opens on the credit side with 900 rupees.
i Sales credited 500 rupees short: Suspense A over c Dr 500 rupees To Sales A over c 500 rupees.
ii Rent debited 400 rupees too much: Suspense A over c Dr 400 rupees To Rent A over c 400 rupees.
Suspense: credit 900; debits 500 plus 400 equals 900. Balance nil, so the account is closed.
So the answer is Suspense Dr 500 divided by Sales Cr 500; Suspense Dr 400 divided by Rent Cr 400; suspense account closes.
